paper.title: Local labour demand and immigrant employment
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement. Acknowledgement (p. 1): …

registers.name_in_paper: the residence permit register (OPHG), provided by the Danish Immigration Service (DIS)
registers.role: sample frame / treatment timing: identifies refugee status without measurement error and the date of residence permit (asylum), which is the date of municipality assignment

linkage / treatment assignment / controls: demographic characteristics and municipality of residence, determined at the end of each year; used to construct the municipality of assignment and relocation
outcomes: employment status in November of each year, 2-4 years since asylum

registers.name_in_paper: information on educational attainment from abroad, obtained through surveys conducted by Statistics Denmark (imputed values excluded and treated as unknown)
registers.role: controls: educational attainment at arrival (0-9, 10-12, more than 12 years, unknown)

registers.name_in_paper: municipality time-series data constructed by the authors, primarily from administrative registers from Statistics Denmark
registers.role: treatment and controls: municipal employment rate, unemployment rate, the same rates amongst non-Western immigrants and amongst low-skilled, employment growth, population share, non-Western immigrant share, co-national share, commuting time/distance to the centre of the local labour market, annual influx of assigned refugees

registers.name_in_paper: internal administrative statistics on the Danish Spatial Dispersal Policy shared by the Danish Immigration Service, and announced municipal refugee quotas
registers.role: sample frame: annual municipal refugee quotas, used to date when each municipality reached its annual quota

linkages: Refugees in the DIS residence permit register linked to the Danish population register and other Statistics Denmark registers via a unique person identifier
Spouses linked to household heads by the partner identifier and the date of asylum (jointly arrived spouses are those who got asylum on the same date as the household head)
Individuals' first registered municipality of residence linked to author-constructed municipality time-series of labour market and demographic characteristics

sample.universe: Newly arrived adult refugees (spontaneous and UN quota refugees) who were granted asylum in Denmark 1999-2010 and were subject to the Danish Spatial Dispersal Policy in place since 1999
sample.unit_of_observation: Individual refugee (household head or jointly arrived spouse), with employment status observed in each of years 2, 3 and 4 since asylum; municipality-year for the persistence regressions in Table A4
selection_rules: All the population in the residence permit register (OPHG) 1997-2016: 1,223,633 observations
Drop observations without a person identifier (pnr): 980,755
Drop individuals with an imputed residence permit type in any year: 776,232
Keep only the first residence permit of each individual: 576,590
Country of origin of the individual or spouse not Denmark: 18,831
Found in the population register (BEF) at least once between 1999 and 2016: 18,176
First appearance in BEF the same year or the year after receiving the residence permit: 12,215 (the gross sample is reported as 12,692 individuals in the text)
Household head (first-arrived adult; the husband if a couple gets asylum on the same date): 9023
Observed in the employment register (RAS) in years 2-4 since asylum: 8479 ('the balanced panel')
Of which received residence permit after 10 municipalities' annual quotas had been filled: 4282 ('the subsample', used in the balancing tests)
Plus refugee spouses of working age who got asylum on the same date as the household head and are observed in RAS in years 2-4: 814
Total 'estimation sample' (household heads and jointly arrived couples): 5096
sample.n_observations: 5096 individuals in the estimation sample (one observation per individual per year since asylum, estimated separately for s = 2, 3, 4); 8479 in the balanced panel; 1568 municipality-years in Table A4
sample.n_individuals: 12,692 gross sample; 8479 balanced panel; 4282 subsample; 5096 estimation sample

construction_notes: The date of municipality assignment is the date of residence permit (asylum) recorded in the residence permit register; the paper also calls it the date of arrival

The first municipality registered in the population register is treated as the municipality of assignment if the refugee is recorded in the registers in the year asylum was granted or the subsequent year

Post-reform municipalities are used throughout; pre-reform municipalities that split are assigned to the post-reform municipality holding the majority of the pre-reform population (13 municipalities affected)
Imputed information on educational attainment from abroad is excluded and the educational level treated as unknown; education acquired in Denmark is not controlled for because it may be endogenous
Employment status is measured in November of each year
Municipality quotas used are those announced and valid on 31 December of the previous year
95 of 98 municipalities are used (3 municipalities, including Copenhagen, had a zero annual quota throughout 1999-2010); the estimation sample spans 94 assigned municipalities
Local employment rate = employed relative to the working-age population; net employment growth = annual change in the number of employed relative to the number employed last year
The cut-off for the estimation sample is arrival after the first 10 municipalities filled their annual quota, chosen as the largest subsample that passes the balancing test
Standard errors are clustered by municipality of assignment (94 clusters) in the individual-level regressions; Tables 1 and A2 use robust standard errors

claims.statement: The employment rate in the current municipality of residence is positively associated with the probability that a refugee is employed 2 years after asylum, in the balanced panel (observational data approach, Eq. (2)).

definition.value: The local employment rate in the municipality of residence in year t+s (number of employed relative to the working-age population, in percent); the current rather than the initial labour demand measure, used to mirror an observational data approach.

timing.value: Year t+s, i.e. s years after asylum, in the current municipality of residence

definition.value: Dummy for the individual being employed in November of year t+s, s = 2, 3 or 4 years since asylum; taken from the employment register (RAS) and estimated as a linear probability model.

timing.value: November of year t+s, s = 2, 3 or 4 years since asylum

units.value: change in the probability of being employed (0-1) per one percentage point higher local employment rate in the current municipality of residence

magnitude.interpretation: The paper reads these as the observational-data benchmark: 0.7-0.8 percentage points in Panel A and 0.6-0.7 in Panel B, above the intent-to-treat estimates of 0.5-0.6 in Panel C, which it interprets as positive self-selection of refugees into municipalities with favourable labour markets

estimand.target_population: The 'balanced panel' of refugee household heads: 8479 newly arrived adult refugees who got asylum 1999-2010, aged 18-59 at arrival, household heads, observed for at least four years since arrival; assigned to 95 municipalities
estimand.formal_query: E[Y_i(t+s) | do(LLM_j(t+s) = x+1)] - E[Y_i(t+s) | do(LLM_j(t+s) = x)], where LLM_j(t+s) is the employment rate in the current municipality of residence

population.description: The 'balanced panel' of refugee household heads: 8479 newly arrived adult refugees who got asylum 1999-2010, aged 18-59 at arrival, household heads, observed for at least four years since arrival; assigned to 95 municipalities
population.period: 1999-2010 (year of asylum); employment outcomes measured 2-4 years later
population.selection: Refugee household heads who got asylum 1999-2010, aged 18-59 at arrival, observed in the employment register in years 2-4 since asylum (no restriction on the calendar month of asylum)

identification.source_of_variation: None beyond conditioning: the current local employment rate in the current municipality of residence, as in an observational data study, estimated to evaluate the direction of the bias from location sorting

key_assumptions.assumption: No self-selection of immigrants into locations in year t+s and no omitted correlated effects (described by the authors as a strong assumption)

lhs: current local employment rate in the municipality of residence (LLM_j(t+s))

implies_edges.to: current local employment rate in the municipality of residence

threats_discussed: Positive self-selection of refugees into municipalities with favourable labour markets, both at arrival and through subsequent relocation
17% of refugees in the estimation sample relocate within four years, and their decision to move is significantly affected by initial local labour market conditions
robustness_checks: Comparison with the intent-to-treat estimates of the initial local employment rate (Table 4, Panel C)
Re-estimation on the uncontaminated estimation sample (Panel B) rather than the balanced panel (Panel A)
unresolved_confounders: Location sorting: the authors state that failure to account for it leads to an upward bias of these estimates

estimation.specification: Eq. (2): OLS/linear probability model of employment status in year t+s on the employment rate in the current municipality of residence in year t+s, with individual characteristics at arrival, current municipality characteristics, and country of origin, year of asylum and month of asylum fixed effects
controls: Educational attainment at arrival (incl. indicator for missing)
estimation.clustering: Standard errors clustered by municipality of assignment (94)

Interaction with a dummy for more than 12 years of education is insignificant (Table 8 Panel C); four years after arrival the interaction has the opposite sign and similar magnitude to the main effect, which the authors interpret as an imprecisely estimated zero effect for high-skilled immigrants, while employment of low-skilled immigrants remains sensitive

definition.value: The local employment rate amongst non-Western immigrants in the municipality of assignment in the year of asylum (t), in percent; an alternative measure of local labour demand for the group the refugees belong to.

timing.value: Year of asylum / municipal assignment (year t)

definition.value: Dummy for the individual being employed in November of year t+s, s = 2, 3 or 4 years since asylum; taken from the employment register (RAS) and estimated as a linear probability model.

timing.value: November of year t+s, s = 2, 3 or 4 years since asylum

units.value: change in the probability of being employed (0-1) per one percentage point higher local employment rate of non-Western immigrants in the municipality of assignment

estimand.target_population: The 'estimation sample': 4282 refugee household heads who got asylum in Denmark 1999-2010 after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual refugee quota, plus their 814 jointly arrived spouses (5096 individuals), assigned to 94 municipalities
estimand.formal_query: E[Y_i(t+s) | do(LLM_j*(t) = x+1)] - E[Y_i(t+s) | do(LLM_j*(t) = x)], where Y is employment status and LLM_j*(t) is the labour demand measure in the municipality of assignment in the year of asylum

population.description: The 'estimation sample': 4282 refugee household heads who got asylum in Denmark 1999-2010 after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual refugee quota, plus their 814 jointly arrived spouses (5096 individuals), assigned to 94 municipalities
population.period: 1999-2010 (year of asylum); employment outcomes measured 2-4 years later
subgroups_defined: more than 12 years of education (high-skilled) vs. less
population.selection: Refugee household heads who got asylum 1999-2010, aged 18-59 at arrival, observed in the employment register in years 2-4 since asylum, who arrived after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual refugee quota in their calendar year of arrival, plus spouses who got asylum on the same date as the household head

identification.source_of_variation: Quasi-random assignment of newly recognised refugees to municipalities under the Danish Spatial Dispersal Policy in place from 1999: annual municipal refugee quotas set by the Danish Immigration Service, exploited for refugees who got asylum after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual quota, when refugees' own settlement preferences can no longer be accommodated

key_assumptions.assumption: Refugees in the sample were randomly distributed across municipalities, conditional on the personal attributes observed by DIS at the time of assignment
key_assumptions.supported_by: Balancing tests of educational attainment against assigned municipality characteristics (Tables 1, A1 Panel E and A2) and the finding that the relocation rate is unrelated to education (Table 2)

lhs: local labour demand in the municipality of assignment (LLM_j*(t))

implies_edges.to: local labour demand in the municipality of assignment

key_assumptions.assumption: No omitted correlated effects: no other characteristic of the local labour market that is correlated with both local labour demand and individual employment is omitted (e.g. city size, job search networks, commuting costs)
key_assumptions.supported_by: Control for the two municipality characteristics used to set the quota and robustness checks adding co-national share, commuting time, commuting distance and commuting area fixed effects (Table 6)

implies_edges.from: omitted local labour market characteristics correlated with local labour demand
implies_edges.to: individual employment status

key_assumptions.assumption: Because the model excludes current labour demand conditions, the initial and current local labour demand conditions must be highly correlated
key_assumptions.supported_by: Time persistency of local labour market conditions: the correlation between the employment rate in year t and t+s (s = 2-4) is 0.85-0.91 (Table A4)

key_assumptions.assumption: The timing of municipal assignment is outside the refugee's control: the month in which asylum is claimed is non-strategic and assignment takes place shortly after asylum is granted
key_assumptions.supported_by: Institutional description and the DIS interview; the cumulative distribution of municipalities that have met their annual quota by calendar month (Fig. 2)

threats_discussed: Self-selection of refugees into locations (location sorting) at the time of arrival, which the design is meant to remove
Subsequent relocation out of the assigned municipality (17% within four years)
Omitted correlated local characteristics: city size, job search networks, commuting costs
Inability to distinguish ITT effects of the current local employment rate from scarring effects
Insufficient within-municipality time variation to include municipality of assignment fixed effects
robustness_checks: Balancing tests of individual characteristics against 12 assigned-municipality characteristics (Table 1) and across cut-offs for the number of filled municipal quotas (Table A1)
Alternative balancing test with educational attainment on the left-hand side (Table A2)
Test that the relocation probability is unrelated to educational attainment (Table 2)
Alternative measures of local labour demand (Table 5) and for low-skilled (Table 7)
Additional municipality controls: co-national share, commuting time/distance, commuting area fixed effects (Table 6)
Alternative cut-offs for the number of municipalities with filled annual quota (Table A6)
Time persistency of local labour market conditions (Table A4)
Split by immigration cohort (Table A7)
unresolved_confounders: The paper cannot distinguish empirically between (ITT) effects of the current local employment rate and scarring effects of the initial local employment rate
Geographical lock-in effects, which the authors say may be substantial

controls: Educational attainment at arrival (incl. indicator for missing)

treatment.label: Unemployment rate of non-Western immigrants at arrival (year t)

definition.value: The local unemployment rate amongst non-Western immigrants in the municipality of assignment in the year of asylum (t), in percent; an alternative measure of local labour demand.

timing.value: Year of asylum / municipal assignment (year t)

definition.value: Dummy for the individual being employed in November of year t+s, s = 2, 3 or 4 years since asylum; taken from the employment register (RAS) and estimated as a linear probability model.

timing.value: November of year t+s, s = 2, 3 or 4 years since asylum

units.value: change in the probability of being employed (0-1) per one percentage point higher local unemployment rate of non-Western immigrants in the municipality of assignment

estimand.target_population: The 'estimation sample': 4282 refugee household heads who got asylum in Denmark 1999-2010 after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual refugee quota, plus their 814 jointly arrived spouses (5096 individuals), assigned to 94 municipalities
estimand.formal_query: E[Y_i(t+s) | do(LLM_j*(t) = x+1)] - E[Y_i(t+s) | do(LLM_j*(t) = x)], where Y is employment status and LLM_j*(t) is the labour demand measure in the municipality of assignment in the year of asylum

population.description: The 'estimation sample': 4282 refugee household heads who got asylum in Denmark 1999-2010 after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual refugee quota, plus their 814 jointly arrived spouses (5096 individuals), assigned to 94 municipalities
population.period: 1999-2010 (year of asylum); employment outcomes measured 2-4 years later
subgroups_defined: more than 12 years of education (high-skilled) vs. less
population.selection: Refugee household heads who got asylum 1999-2010, aged 18-59 at arrival, observed in the employment register in years 2-4 since asylum, who arrived after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual refugee quota in their calendar year of arrival, plus spouses who got asylum on the same date as the household head

identification.source_of_variation: Quasi-random assignment of newly recognised refugees to municipalities under the Danish Spatial Dispersal Policy in place from 1999: annual municipal refugee quotas set by the Danish Immigration Service, exploited for refugees who got asylum after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual quota, when refugees' own settlement preferences can no longer be accommodated

key_assumptions.assumption: Refugees in the sample were randomly distributed across municipalities, conditional on the personal attributes observed by DIS at the time of assignment
key_assumptions.supported_by: Balancing tests of educational attainment against assigned municipality characteristics (Tables 1, A1 Panel E and A2) and the finding that the relocation rate is unrelated to education (Table 2)

lhs: local labour demand in the municipality of assignment (LLM_j*(t))

implies_edges.to: local labour demand in the municipality of assignment

key_assumptions.assumption: No omitted correlated effects: no other characteristic of the local labour market that is correlated with both local labour demand and individual employment is omitted (e.g. city size, job search networks, commuting costs)
key_assumptions.supported_by: Control for the two municipality characteristics used to set the quota and robustness checks adding co-national share, commuting time, commuting distance and commuting area fixed effects (Table 6)

implies_edges.from: omitted local labour market characteristics correlated with local labour demand
implies_edges.to: individual employment status

key_assumptions.assumption: Because the model excludes current labour demand conditions, the initial and current local labour demand conditions must be highly correlated
key_assumptions.supported_by: Time persistency of local labour market conditions: the correlation between the employment rate in year t and t+s (s = 2-4) is 0.85-0.91 (Table A4)

key_assumptions.assumption: The timing of municipal assignment is outside the refugee's control: the month in which asylum is claimed is non-strategic and assignment takes place shortly after asylum is granted
key_assumptions.supported_by: Institutional description and the DIS interview; the cumulative distribution of municipalities that have met their annual quota by calendar month (Fig. 2)

threats_discussed: Self-selection of refugees into locations (location sorting) at the time of arrival, which the design is meant to remove
Subsequent relocation out of the assigned municipality (17% within four years)
Omitted correlated local characteristics: city size, job search networks, commuting costs
Inability to distinguish ITT effects of the current local employment rate from scarring effects
Insufficient within-municipality time variation to include municipality of assignment fixed effects
robustness_checks: Balancing tests of individual characteristics against 12 assigned-municipality characteristics (Table 1) and across cut-offs for the number of filled municipal quotas (Table A1)
Alternative balancing test with educational attainment on the left-hand side (Table A2)
Test that the relocation probability is unrelated to educational attainment (Table 2)
Alternative measures of local labour demand (Table 5) and for low-skilled (Table 7)
Additional municipality controls: co-national share, commuting time/distance, commuting area fixed effects (Table 6)
Alternative cut-offs for the number of municipalities with filled annual quota (Table A6)
Time persistency of local labour market conditions (Table A4)
Split by immigration cohort (Table A7)
unresolved_confounders: The paper cannot distinguish empirically between (ITT) effects of the current local employment rate and scarring effects of the initial local employment rate
Geographical lock-in effects, which the authors say may be substantial

definition.value: Dummy for the individual being employed in November of year t+s, s = 2, 3 or 4 years since asylum; taken from the employment register (RAS) and estimated as a linear probability model.

timing.value: November of year t+s, s = 2, 3 or 4 years since asylum

units.value: change in the probability of being employed (0-1) per one percentage point higher local employment growth in the municipality of assignment

ambiguities: The abstract states 83% four years after assignment, while the text on p. 3 states that 89% still live in the municipality of assignment by the end of the third year and 76% by the end of the fourth year; the 83% figure cannot be located exactly on Fig. 1's axis, so the value is transcribed from the abstract.
The treatment here is policy exposure itself, not a labour demand measure: this is a descriptive survivor rate, not a regression.
The 'sign' field does not really apply: the quantity is a level (a survivor rate), not an estimated effect, so sign is recorded as positive with low confidence.
